page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 77 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, though it does not include any bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves a strong single-core stress-ng CPU score of 2701.48, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. However, its multi-core stress-ng performance and Geekbench multi-core score of 2149.0 fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical limitation of its single-core, dual-thread layout. Memory bandwidth is also a notable bottleneck; read-only small block cached bandwidth is poor at 140.21 GB/sec, while large block read and write bandwidths remain weak at 34.27 GB/sec and 22.5 GB/sec respectively.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. While single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, database operations and redis SET operations score poorly, with redis achieving 2.27 million operations per second. The E2ads_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications requiring a small CPU footprint, such as lightweight caching layers, simple relational databases, or basic text processing tasks, but is poorly suited for software compilation, physics simulations, or LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it includes 77 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, with no integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks show a strong single-core stress-ng CPU score in the top 25%, but multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth are limited, falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Single-threaded tasks like text processing and compression perform at average levels, whereas database operations, software compilation, and redis SET operations show poor throughput. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive, low-concurrency workloads such as lightweight caching, small databases, or basic text processing.
